summary:
EASD 2026 in Milan (29 Sep–2 Oct) has set off the biggest GLP-1 news cycle of the quarter. The best opportunities over the next 72 hours are the new results that just came out. First is Lilly's eloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide), a Phase 2 trial in adults with type 2 diabetes plus obesity or overweight, published today: about 54 lb lost on the top dose vs 34.4 lb (14.8%) on tirzepatide 15 mg alone at 48 weeks (n=367). It has heavy trade and news coverage but almost no creator explainers yet. Second is the full retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 paper in The Lancet: 20.8% on 12 mg at 80 weeks, n=1,152. Headlines are quoting 18.8%, 20.8%, 21% and even 30%, which suits a headline decoder, the format that has worked best for us. Third is Zealand's amylin drug petrelintide (ZUPREME-1, Lancet D&E): about 10% at 42 weeks, with side effects similar to placebo. This gives us a simple 'what is amylin?' explainer that ties the whole amylin wave together (eloraTZP, CagriSema, petrelintide).

The Lilly vs Novo 'indirect comparison war' is producing claims that fit our 'Did X really beat Y?' titles: Zepbound vs Wegovy HD 7.2 mg, Foundayo vs oral semaglutide 25 mg, and Ozempic 2 mg vs switching to Mounjaro on heart risk. Each needs a clear 'not a head-to-head trial, company-sponsored' framing, and no switching advice. The Wegovy pill real-world data (OCTANE: 4.1% at 3 months after switching from injections) is getting mainstream pickup from Reuters and CNBC.

Topics carried over from earlier snapshots:
- The pancreatic cancer reassurance is still rising, now with a second global cohort.
- The stopping-GLP-1 heart-risk story is now on TV news (Scripps).
- The SELECT mediation story is fading.

The children's nutritional deficiency study (16.8%) and Fox's 'starve the brain' claim are useful 'eat well on GLP-1' hooks if framed carefully. I've rejected two items:
- 'Can patients on GLP-1s stop insulin?', because it's medication-change bait.
- GLP-1 misuse in eating disorders, because it's a guardrail risk.

Competition is uniformly low for our niche's explanatory angle because most coverage so far is investor or trade press.

candidates.topic: EloraTZP (eloralintide + tirzepatide) vs tirzepatide 15 mg: ~54 lb vs 34.4 lb (14.8%) average weight loss at 48 weeks in adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity/overweight (Phase 2, n=367, EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Did Lilly's new combo really beat Mounjaro?' Explain what amylin adds on top of tirzepatide (fullness, slower eating), give the top-dose vs tirzepatide-15-mg numbers with population and timeframe, the A1C drop (up to 2.9% vs 2.4%), more GI side effects, and that it's Phase 2 and not approved. Phase 3 comes next.
candidates.why_now: Presented and press-released today (30 Sep) at EASD. Reuters, STAT, CNBC, Fierce, MarketWatch and qz all ran it within hours, but there are almost no creator explainers yet. The drug name is brand-new, so search demand starts from zero and will spike as TikTok picks it up.

evidence.signal: Up to 23.3% weight loss at top dose; greater weight loss and A1C reduction vs tirzepatide 15 mg in obesity + T2D
48-week Phase 2, 367 participants; top dose 54.1 lb vs 34.4 lb (14.8%) tirzepatide alone; A1C −2.9% vs −2.4%
Mainstream health-news pickup the same day

candidates.topic: Retatrutide TRIUMPH-2 full results in The Lancet: up to 20.8% average weight loss (12 mg) vs placebo at 80 weeks in 1,152 adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity/overweight
candidates.angle: Headline decoder: 'Retatrutide: 18.8%, 20.8%, 21% or 30%? Which number is real?' Explain the two estimands (everyone randomized vs people who stayed on the drug), name the population (T2D, so less weight loss than trials without diabetes), A1C −1.6 points, and the side effects (nausea and diarrhea, AE discontinuation 3.8–11.6% vs 4.9% placebo). Not approved yet.
candidates.why_now: The Lancet paper and EASD symposium landed 29–30 Sep, with Time, NBC, USA Today, SciAm and the Guardian ('Godzilla') all covering it. Outlets are quoting different numbers (18.8% vs 20.8% vs 30%), which is exactly the confusion our decoder format pays off. The topic is accelerating in our snapshots (86→92).

evidence.signal: Up to 49.6 lb (20.8%) average loss and A1C −1.6% at 80 weeks
Phase 3 double-blind RCT published 29 Sep 2026
Reports 'up to 18.8%', a different estimand than the 20.8% headline
1,152 randomized 1:1:1:1; GI AEs and discontinuation rates

candidates.topic: What is amylin? Petrelintide (ZUPREME-1, Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology): ~9–11% weight loss at 42 weeks vs placebo, with side effects comparable to placebo (Phase 2, n=485)
candidates.angle: Mechanism explainer: 'The next wave isn't only GLP-1: meet amylin, your fullness hormone.' Tie petrelintide, eloraTZP and CagriSema together, explain why amylin drugs may be gentler on the stomach, and state clearly that it's Phase 2 and not approved.
candidates.why_now: Published in the Lancet D&E on 29 Sep, plus a Medical Xpress feature today. Three amylin stories are converging at EASD (eloraTZP, CagriSema analyses, petrelintide), so 'what is amylin' searches should build over the week. Very few consumer explainers exist.

evidence.signal: Up to ~10% weight loss with adverse events comparable to placebo
485 participants, 42 weeks; 8.7–10.7% by dose vs placebo; 34–56% lost ≥10%
'Offering potential alternative to GLP-1 therapies'
ZUPREME 1 randomized double-blind Phase 2

candidates.topic: Did Zepbound really beat Wegovy HD (7.2 mg)? Lilly's indirect comparison: 4.5% more weight loss with tirzepatide 15 mg at 72 weeks (SURMOUNT-1 vs STEP UP, not head-to-head)
candidates.angle: 'Did X really beat Y?' decoder. Explain what an indirect treatment comparison is (two separate trials, statistically adjusted), who funded it (Lilly), what it found (4.5% / 3.2%, >3× odds of ≥20% loss, no significant A1C difference, similar AE discontinuation), and why a randomized head-to-head trial is stronger. No switching advice.
keywords: Mounjaro vs Ozempic which is better
candidates.why_now: The press release came out 29 Sep, and BioSpace framed it as Lilly 'building a commercial case with indirect analyses'. 'Zepbound vs Ozempic' is a high-volume evergreen search (Forbes ran an explainer today), and the fresh number refreshes it.

evidence.signal: Tirzepatide 10/15 mg associated with more weight loss than semaglutide 7.2 mg in an indirect comparison
4.5% and 3.2% advantage (treatment-regimen estimand) at 72 weeks; covariate-adjusted
Independent indirect comparison of tirzepatide vs semaglutide in people without T2D

candidates.topic: Switching from GLP-1 shots to the Wegovy pill (oral semaglutide): average 4.1% further weight loss at 3 months in real-world OCTANE data (EASD 2026)
candidates.angle: 'Does the Wegovy pill work as well as the shot?' Set out what OCTANE shows (real-world, Novo-sponsored, 3 months, no comparison group, adults switching from injectable semaglutide or tirzepatide) and what it can't show. Point to trial data for the pill, and end with questions to ask your prescriber. No advice to switch.
candidates.why_now: Reuters, CNBC, Yahoo, Everyday Health and qz all covered it on 30 Sep. Pill-vs-shot is one of the most-asked GLP-1 questions, and Ro and Novo just announced a real-world evidence partnership.

evidence.signal: OCTANE: 4.1% average loss at 3 months after switching from injectable semaglutide/tirzepatide
Company release; ~41% lost ≥5%
Mainstream wire pickup

candidates.topic: Semaglutide not linked to pancreatic cancer or pancreatitis: Nordic registry (EASD) plus a new global propensity-matched cohort in type 2 diabetes (J Pers Med)
candidates.angle: Myth-bust: 'Does Ozempic cause pancreatic cancer?' Two large independent datasets say no link was found. Use 'not linked', not 'proven safe'. Explain observational limits and name the pancreatitis warning symptoms, with severe tummy pain spreading to the back = call 911/999 or go to ER/A&E.
candidates.why_now: Seen in 5 snapshots at a steady 80. News-Medical picked it up on 29 Sep, a second independent cohort just published, and cancer-worry searches ('does tirzepatide cause cancer') appear in today's feeds.

evidence.signal: Registry data: semaglutide not linked to pancreatic cancer
GLP-1 RAs not associated with increased acute pancreatitis or pancreatic cancer in T2D (global propensity-matched cohort)

candidates.topic: Did Ozempic 2 mg really beat switching to Mounjaro on heart risk? Novo's real-world COMPETE SWITCH CV: adjusted HR 1.06 (6% higher MACE risk) in those who switched to tirzepatide vs escalated semaglutide, in adults with T2D
candidates.angle: Headline decoder that puts both company stories side by side. Novo's observational data favors semaglutide 2 mg on heart events, while another EASD real-world analysis favors tirzepatide on glucose and weight. Explain observational confounding, industry funding, and that SURPASS-CVOT is the RCT evidence. Strictly no dose or switching advice.
keywords: which GLP-1 is better for heart
candidates.why_now: PR Newswire 29 Sep plus HCPLive, Benzinga, Cardiovascular Business and Korea Biomedical today. The 'Novo vs Lilly' framing is everywhere at EASD. It builds on our proven 'CagriSema vs tirzepatide' decoder format.

evidence.signal: Adjusted HR 1.06 (1.04–1.08); 185,705 escalated vs 23,104 switched
Company release on the real-world analysis
Counter-analysis: tirzepatide outperforms semaglutide in real-world T2D

candidates.topic: Foundayo (orforglipron) 17.2 mg vs oral semaglutide 25 mg: 1.5–2.4% more weight loss and 0.3–0.6% more A1C reduction in adults with T2D (indirect comparison, ACHIEVE-3 vs PIONEER PLUS)
candidates.angle: 'Which GLP-1 pill works better?' Explain both pills, what the indirect comparison found, that oral semaglutide 25 mg isn't FDA-approved for T2D (as of Sept 2026), and orforglipron's higher GI side-effect and discontinuation rates in earlier head-to-head data. Continues our orforglipron coverage.
candidates.why_now: Lilly release 29 Sep, plus Pharmacy Times and Pharmaceutical Technology today. The GLP-1 pill era is a top audience question, and it pairs with the Wegovy pill switch data for a 'pill vs pill' carousel.

evidence.signal: Orforglipron edges oral semaglutide 25 mg in indirect comparison
1.5% more weight loss, 0.3% more A1C reduction; 25 mg not US-approved for T2D

candidates.topic: Stopping GLP-1 medicines linked to higher heart attack, stroke and death risk: up to 22% higher after 2 years off, in 333,000+ US veterans with T2D (BMJ Medicine)
candidates.angle: 'What happens to your heart when you stop a GLP-1?' Give the observational finding with its exact population, and reframe it positively: why staying on track with your prescriber matters, plus habits that help protect results. Explicitly no stopping or changing advice; plan any change with your clinician.
keywords: what happens when you stop GLP-1
candidates.why_now: Seen in 4 snapshots (84→76, still high), and it's now on local and TV news (Scripps, 30 Sep). Mainstream reach means searches are still climbing even as trade coverage fades.

evidence.signal: 'Stopping GLP-1 drugs may raise heart attack and stroke risk'

candidates.topic: Nearly 1 in 6 (16.8%) children aged 10–17 starting GLP-1s were diagnosed with a nutritional deficiency within a year; vitamin D most common (12.4%); only 5% got nutrition counseling within 30 days (Childhood Obesity, n=2,031)
candidates.angle: 'Eating well on a GLP-1: what this kids' study teaches everyone.' State the exact population (adolescents, US records, diagnosis-coded, observational), then give evidence-based nutrition priorities on GLP-1 (protein, vitamin D, fiber, a dietitian referral), with the protein caveat. No fear framing.
candidates.why_now: The paper came out 17 Sep, and the ScienceDaily/US News wave (23–24 Sep) is now reaching SciTechDaily, Men's Journal and local TV (30 Sep). This is the mainstream diffusion stage. 'Nutrients on GLP-1' is a strong evergreen search.

evidence.signal: 16.8% diagnosed with a nutritional deficiency in year 1
2,031 patients aged 10–17; vitamin D 12.4%; counseling rates

candidates.topic: 'Can GLP-1 drugs starve your brain?' Decoding the Fox News expert warning on rapid weight loss and brain energy
candidates.angle: Myth decode: it's an expert's opinion (Dr. Tommy Wood, UW) drawn from undereating and marathon research, not a new GLP-1 study. Cover what human evidence exists and what doesn't, why eating enough protein, iron and omega-3 matters on GLP-1, and emerging brain-health research. Calm and positive.
candidates.why_now: Fox published it today (30 Sep), and it's being syndicated to dozens of local radio sites. Fear headlines like this spread fast on TikTok, so being first with a calm, evidence-based decode helps.

evidence.signal: Expert warns rapid weight loss could 'starve' the brain; notes drugs may also bring cognitive benefits
Neurological complications with rapid weight loss plus nutritional deficiencies after GLP-1 use (single case)

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and migraine: women used 8% fewer triptans a year after starting semaglutide for weight loss (Danish nationwide, 189,392 people, Novo co-sponsored, observational)
candidates.angle: Benefits-beyond-weight explainer: 'Could Wegovy help migraines?' Say 'linked to' and cover the sex difference (no change in men), why GLP-1 might affect headache pressure, and the limits (medication use as a proxy, sponsorship).
candidates.why_now: Clinical Pain Advisor re-surfaced it on 30 Sep, and Healthline covered it. Migraine is a high-search condition, few GLP-1 creators have covered it, and it fits the 'beyond weight' pillar.

evidence.signal: 7% reduction overall, 8% in women, no change in men; 189,392 initiators
Interrupted time series paper

candidates.topic: Protecting muscle on GLP-1s: lean mass is ~20–30% of weight lost, and what protein, strength training (and possibly creatine) can do (Clin Nutr commentary; creatine RCT underway)
candidates.angle: Practical, positive: 'Losing muscle on Ozempic? Here's what actually helps.' Lead with strength training plus protein (with the kidney caveat). Present creatine honestly as promising but still being tested in GLP-1 users (NCT07625202). No supplement dosing hype.
candidates.why_now: The Clin Nutr piece 'Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss' (21 Sep) plus a newly registered RCT refresh a top evergreen question. It's a playbook double-down topic.

evidence.signal: Creatine for GLP-1-associated muscle loss
Creatine supplementation during GLP-1a therapy trial
GLP-1 RAs and muscle mass measures

candidates.topic: CagriSema changes brain responses to food cues and reduces organ fat (new EASD analyses)
candidates.angle: Mechanism: 'How CagriSema quiets the brain's response to food pictures', worded as measured brain responses (not 'food noise'), with study size and status. Links to the amylin wave.
candidates.why_now: Patient Care Online covered it on 30 Sep. It continues our CagriSema Short (one of our GLP-1 winners), and the amylin theme is peaking this week.

evidence.source: Patient Care Online via Google News
evidence.signal: CagriSema alters food-cue responses, reduces organ fat in new analyses

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide dull pleasure? Semaglutide altered reward-seeking behavior in healthy mice (PsyPost)
candidates.angle: Search-style decoder, following our winning 'only in mice' format: 'Does Ozempic make you enjoy things less?' Say what the mouse study showed, what human data exists on mood, and that it's not proven in humans.
candidates.why_now: PsyPost story on 30 Sep. The 'Ozempic killed my joy' question circulates on Reddit and TikTok, and the playbook shows honest mouse-study decoders perform well.

evidence.signal: Semaglutide alters reward-seeking behavior in healthy mice
GLP-1 RA use and new depression diagnoses in Medicaid adults with T2D (human observational context)

candidates.topic: GLP-1s and hair, skin and nails: what's common, what's linked to fast weight loss, and what helps
candidates.angle: Side-effect explainer continuing our hair-loss long-form (top 2): cover the mechanisms (telogen effluvium from rapid weight loss, nutrition) and evidence-based habits, and say when to see a clinician. Add the new melanoma/skin cancer cohort only as 'no increased risk found' if the paper supports it.
candidates.why_now: Yahoo Health ran an explainer on 30 Sep, and a new propensity-matched skin-cancer cohort was published 27 Sep. This is a perennial high-volume search.

evidence.signal: How can GLP-1 drugs affect hair, skin and nails?
GLP-1 RAs and melanoma/nonmelanoma skin cancer risk cohort

candidates.topic: Safe disposal of used GLP-1 pens and needles: local warnings as injection use grows
candidates.angle: Practical 'life on GLP-1' Short: how to dispose of pens and needles safely (FDA-cleared sharps container, or a heavy-duty plastic household container if none is available; check local rules). Keep the wording matched to FDA guidance.
candidates.why_now: Central Oregon Daily warned about used GLP-1 needles on 30 Sep. It's a practical question with little creator coverage.

evidence.source: Central Oregon Daily via Google News
evidence.signal: Warnings about used needles from GLP-1 drugs

candidates.topic: Weight loss explains only ~20% of semaglutide's heart benefit (SELECT mediation analysis, European Heart Journal)
candidates.angle: Only with a fresh angle: combine it with retatrutide and eloraTZP ('bigger weight loss ≠ proven bigger heart benefit yet') using the SELECT population (adults with established CVD plus overweight/obesity).
candidates.why_now: Seen in 7 snapshots with momentum declining (72→56). It's only useful as supporting context for the new next-gen drug news.

evidence.signal: SELECT mediation analysis

candidates.topic: 'Can patients on GLP-1s stop taking insulin?' (Medscape)
candidates.angle: Not recommended: the core question is a medication-stopping decision. If it's covered at all, it should only be as 'GLP-1s and insulin work differently; any change is your diabetes team's call', and that's better folded into other content.
candidates.why_now: Medscape clinician piece, 30 Sep. It's high-risk bait for medication-change advice.

evidence.signal: Can patients on GLP-1s stop taking insulin?

candidates.topic: GLP-1 drugs misused by patients with eating disorders (ABC7 study coverage)
candidates.angle: Rejected for this automated pipeline: high risk of ED-adjacent framing and weight-focused imagery. Revisit only with human editorial review and support resources.
candidates.why_now: ABC7 coverage on 30 Sep. It conflicts with the brand's eating-disorder guardrail.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 drugs may be misused by patients with eating disorders
